newsitem.title: USA: American International to build air cargo center.
newsitem.headline: American International to build air cargo center.

text.p: American International Freight, an overnight, scheduled air cargo operation that services 45 U.S. cities, said Monday it is negotiating with the Fort Wayne-Allen County Airport Authority to build a new air cargo hub on 75 acres at the Fort Wayne International Airport.

"The Airport Authority will seek its board's approval for a bond proposal, conduct public hearings this spring, and, if all goes as planned, will sign the final papers this summer," said American International Vice President and General Manager Stephen Murray.
"Construction could begin as early as this fall," he said in a statement.

The proposed bond issue, for $33.5 million, will be used to construct the new facilities. Some 75 acres of land will be cleared for construction, including 35 acres of ramps for aircraft parking, 33 acres of buildings and seven acres of landscaping.
American International, owned by race car driver Conrad Kalitta, plans to move its entire hub operation from Terre Haute, Ind. to Fort Wayne in late 1998.
The Terre Haute facility has 350 employees. Some 300-400 job openings are projected for the Fort Wayne facility.

American International's current hub has only 100,000 square feet of buildings, with planes spread out over a large area resulting in longer times to move freight from the planes to the sorting facility, Murray said.
After an extensive survey of potential sites, the company said it chose Fort Wayne because of the geographic advantages it offers and the economic benefits realized from the proposal.
